partner_verdicts.rationale: SMB bookkeeping automation is a large, underserved category and the timing is right — QuickBooks/Xero haven't moved fast on AI-native workflows. Early traction (300 customers, 18% MoM) suggests real category-creation pull.

Strong product-market fit signals with 300 paying customers and 18% MoM MRR growth. However, the GTM motion (inbound + accountant partnerships) isn't quantified by channel, so it's unclear how repeatable this is beyond the founders.

Unit economics are emerging but not yet proven at scale. $400K ARR at 300 customers implies ~$1,333 ACV, consistent with the stated $150/mo pricing, but no LTV/CAC or gross margin figures were shared.

exchanges.position: The category-timing story is compelling but it's not GTM proof without channel-level economics — I'd want the same evidence before calling this repeatable.
I don't discount the category-timing thesis, but a timing bet doesn't substitute for a gross-margin figure — those are answering different questions.
Agreed the channel mix isn't proven yet, but 18% MoM with zero paid spend is still a strong category-pull signal even before we see per-channel CAC.
Agreed on needing channel-level CAC before committing — that would also sharpen the LTV/CAC picture I'm missing. (concedes this point)
Fair point on unit economics being unproven — I'd still weight the category timing bet heavily, but I don't dispute we need the numbers. (concedes this point)
Agreed we need cohort and margin data before committing — that reinforces rather than changes my position.

key_concerns: Category timing bets are inherently hard to verify this early
No named incumbent has publicly failed at this yet, so the 'why now' is inferred rather than evidenced
GTM motion is described but not proven — no channel-level economics
Unclear if the accountant-partnership channel is repeatable beyond the founders' existing relationships
No churn analysis shared — need cohort data
No LTV/CAC or gross margin figures disclosed
18-month runway claim not yet cross-checked against burn rate
diligence_requirements: Competitive teardown of QuickBooks/Xero AI roadmap
3 customer reference calls on why they switched
Cohort retention curves (monthly, by acquisition channel)
Full unit economics workup (LTV/CAC, gross margin, payback period)
